why: Because each part may be rearranged, a part works iff its counts can be balanced: '?' must cover |#( - #)| + |#[ - #]| and the leftover '?' count must be even. Prefix counts of the five characters give both parts' counts at every split in O(1).
hints: Rearranging removes all ordering constraints. What must be true of the counts of each bracket type in a part?
A part is fixable iff q >= |open( - close)| + |open[ - close]| and (q minus that) is even, since leftover '?' must pair up as () or [].
Sweep split points 1..n-1 keeping running counts for the left part; the right part is totals minus left. Count splits where both sides pass. O(n).
pitfalls: Parity matters: one leftover '?' cannot be used, so an odd remainder fails.
Treat the two bracket types separately; a '(' cannot be matched by ']'.
